sample_unit: patients (79 Yale analytical/development cohort; 215 Swedish prognostic validation cohort)
models_evaluated: seven newly developed AI TIL scoring models
three previously validated AI TIL models

links.outcome: Comparison of ten AI TIL models on analytical and prognostic validity against invasive disease-free survival
links.effect: Analytical validity differed across models (Spearman's r = 0.63-0.73, p < 0.001); eight of ten models were prognostic with overlapping HR = 0.40-0.47 (p < 0.004) in external cohort.
links.quote: A significant difference in analytical validity (Spearman's r = 0.63-0.73, p < 0.001) is highlighted across AI methodologies and training strategies.

links.outcome: Prognostic performance of AI TIL models in independent external cohort
links.effect: Eight of ten AI models showed prognostic validity in the external Swedish cohort (HR = 0.40-0.47; p < 0.004), while analytical validity differed across models.
links.quote: Interestingly, the prognostic performance of digital TILs is demonstrated for eight out of ten AI models, even less extensively trained ones, with similar and overlapping hazard ratios (HR) in the external validation cohort (Cox regression analysis based on IDFS-endpoint, HR = 0.40-0.47; p < 0.004).

unlisted_practices: Establishing a large multi-centric benchmark dataset to ensure comparability of different AI tools for the same task

screen.reason: Evaluates analytical and prognostic validity across multiple AI models for scoring tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in breast cancer histopathology, but does not test a specific clinical deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
